question: How do light-dependent reactions provide the energy carriers used by the Calvin cycle?

local_edit_geometry.replacement: Photosystems absorb light and use electron transport chains to convert energy into chemical energy [ev_002]. Photosystem I absorbs a second photon, resulting in the formation of NADPH, an energy carrier for the Calvin cycle reactions [ev_010]. After energy from the sun is converted into chemical energy and temporarily stored in ATP and NADPH molecules, the cell has the fuel needed to build carbohydrate molecules for long-term energy storage [ev_003].
